pages.text: Looking at my options, I may want to start crafting sturdier building blocks to reinforce my structures. Before I gain access to a $(l:innovation/machines/stonecutter)stonecutter$(), I could consider laying down $(thing)rammed earth$() or $(thing)dry fitted stone$(). But I could also invest into earthware like $(thing)mud, clay$() or $(thing)adobe bricks$().

$(italics)$(#a84b0f)Right clicking with a crowbar will $(bold)instantly$(italics)$(#a84b0f) remove any resilient base-defense building block. This includes mortared bricks, nailed planks, rammed earth, and dry fitted stone$(br2)There are mason picks that are more durable as well.$()

Rammed earth is surprisingly easy to make, if labor-intensive. Compressing $(thing)three dirt blocks$() of any type in a $(l:innovation/advanced_crafting/compacting_bin)compacting bin$() will result in a single, resistant block.
Dry fitted stone can make for highly-efficient walls, made from carefully stacked $(thing)rocks$() pressed down by gravity. It is... surprisingly easy to make? Why do I feel like this won't last.

pages.title: Plain Glazed Bricks
pages.text: Bricks made from glazed materials such as mud, clay, or adobe, I can create without a stonecutter. They are decently solid, but like stone bricks, they require $(t:Can be searched in JEI. Includes clay balls, slime, refractory material...)$(item)mortar$() to stick together.

pages.title: Plain Stone Bricks
pages.text: Bricks made from stone are among the toughest there are; however, their hardness is dependent on the type of rock, which I can confirm individually by checking blocks of stone or cobbleston. They require $(t:Can be searched in JEI. Includes clay balls, slime, refractory material...)$(item)mortar$()

pages.title: Advanced Glazed Bricks
pages.text: If I approach glazed bricks from a different approach, pure, solid porcelain bricks would work fantastic for a hard barrier. Refractory bricks would be up there, but from what I've gathered, there might be an even harder, if less tough material in the nether part of the world.
I'm not really capable of reproducing this substance. It might just be the most durable material I've ever seen employed in building, barring anomalies like worldspines or onyx.
